articleTitle: An Adaptive Local Context Extraction Method for Motion Prediction and Planning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: Learning-based motion prediction and planning algorithms can efficiently extract and effectively represent the agent-map relationships in high-dimensional space. Generally, the performance is highly related to the neural network structure and quality of input data. However, existing works are more focused on exploring novel network structures while ignoring the form of data input. Typically, for a target agent to predict or plan, they simply input all road polylines within its R-meters radius as local context information and then use a network such as a cross-attention module to filter out the unimportant and irrelevant part of the local context. This simple strategy not only burdens the network in spatial and temporal computation consumption but also leads to much redundancy and overlapping when two target agents are very close. We propose our Adaptive Breadth-First Search (ABFS) local context extraction method to tackle these issues. ABFS inherits from breadth-first search (BFS), adding adaptive search depth based on the agent’s current state and changing the weights of the search direction (more focused on the roads forward). We compare our methods with previous radius search (RS) based and depth-first search (DFS) based context extraction methods. Systematic experiments are done based on the Differentiable Integrated Motion Prediction and Planning (DIPP) algorithm using Waymo motion dataset. We give both qualitative and quantitative results to show our method’s superiority.

articleTitle: Object Recognition System under Hazy Condition for Automated Driving Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: We propose an object recognition system for vehicles controlled by "Automated Driving Systems (ADS)." In particular, the proposed system aims at operating "Minimum Risk Maneuver (MRM)" for the ADS only with image sensors. The image sensors, digital cameras for example, often face difficulties in acquiring images with foggy, rainy and/or misty weather conditions. Even in such "Hazy" conditions, the object recognition system should be reliable to perform the MRM strategy. The proposed system consists of two sub-systems: image "dehaze" processing, and object detection. The implemented system was validated by several sample movies recorded in hazy condition on real roads. Experimental results show that the proposed system is applicable to real-time applications.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Shopping Cart with Automatic Following Function
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: The global impact of the Covid-19 outbreak has threatened the social and economic fabric of the communities, and altered the nature of lives. Today, as the major health risks of COVID-19 seem to be receding, it is crucial to pause, ponder and plan to progress after the crisis to be better prepared for the future. In view of the rising of physical retail transactions, it is noticed that the physical shopping crowd has returned since people loathed the feeling of being cooped up in the house during movement control orders. As such, a contactless intelligent shopping cart could be an ideal invention. This paper aims to design and develop an intelligent shopping cart with an automatic following function, which is capable of trailing shoppers while avoiding obstacles along the way with its built-in obstacle detection function. The proposed design embeds renewable energy technology into the cart by using solar-charged batteries to power up the sensors and controllers on the cart. The results show that the successful prototype fulfils the objectives of extending convenience to people from the perspective of social, environmental and health for the sustainable development of tomorrow.

articleTitle: 4DRT-SLAM: Robust SLAM in Smoke Environments using 4D Radar and Thermal Camera based on Dense Deep Learnt Features
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: LiDAR- and Visual- SLAM are prone to fail in smoke and fog environments, because LiDAR and visual camera cannot penetrate smoke and fog. Fortunately, both 4D radar (x, y, z, velocity) and thermal camera can work robustly in such adverse conditions. However, little related work has been performed. In this paper, 4DRT-SLAM is presented, where 4D radar and thermal camera are fused to perform the SLAM in smoke and fog conditions. Since the point cloud of 4D radar is rather sparse and noisy, it is difficult to extract valid geometric features (line and plane). In 4DRT-SLAM, firstly, we perform 2D feature extraction and matching on thermal images. Considering that hand-crafted features do not work well for thermal images, we use deep-learned features (LoFTR). Secondly, the corresponding 3D coordinates of these feature points are obtained by projecting the point cloud of 4D radar onto thermal image, with the intrinsic and extrinsic parameters. Thirdly, Perspective-n-Point (PnP) is performed to calculate the transformation matrix between two consecutive frames. Experiments are performed in real smoke environments. Both quantitative and qualitative analyses demonstrate that 4DRT-SLAM is effective and robust in smoke environments.

articleTitle: A Dataset for Object Detection in Night Rainy Scenes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: Object detection is a fundamental task in computer vision. As the datasets for object detection are constructed, deep learning approaches are leveraged to show promising results. However, most of the existing datasets are aimed at normal weather scenarios, which limits the use of the trained neural networks in normal conditions. Recently, some datasets cover the night samples or rainy samples though, rare samples are utilized to focus on the night rainy scenarios. As we evaluate, the night effects and rainy effects are not decoupled. They result in a more complicated problem, thus a need for a night rainy dataset is raised to boost the deep learning tools in the data aspect. Besides, we collect the rainfall rate with a rain gauge to measure the rain intensity, splitting the dataset according to the rain intensity so that the networks can be trained according to different rainfall rates. Our whole dataset contains more than 3000 samples, with 4865 objects labeled. Specifically, the dataset contains 5 classes labeled as pedestrian, car, bus, truck, and motor cyclist. To show the effectiveness of the dataset, we use the latest detection algorithm trained on the open dataset and our dataset for comparison. The significant improvement reveals that our dataset are unique and strongly pushes the networks to the practical useful end.

articleTitle: Abnormal Automated Guided Vehicles Detection for Fleet Management Systems: A Reputation-based Distributed Velocity Estimation Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: Fleet management systems usually require many automated guided vehicles (AGVs) work together to carry out one specific task. Due to the complexity of factory environments and the unreliability of onboard sensors/actuators, the AGVs may be compromised when executing tasks. To timely detect the abnormal AGVs, this paper proposes a reputation-based distributed velocity estimation approach. In this approach, each AGV can distinguish its neighbors’ abnormal behaviors by the unreasonable velocities estimated from the communication network. The convergence of this approach is analyzed based on the remaining communication topology after isolating the abnormal AGVs. Validations of the proposed approach are conducted under different categories of faults, and the results demonstrate its feasibility in abnormal AGV detection for fleet management systems.

articleTitle: Traffic Incident Generation And Supervised Learning Based Detection Via A Microscopic Simulation Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: An effective automatic incident detection (AID) method is vital in the intelligent transportation system. This paper presents an online Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based traffic incident detection method to detect the incidents in urban networks by three types of traffic flow data (traffic volume, speed and acceleration of vehicles). Regarding the traffic flow data during a time period as an image with RGB channels, this method employs the idea of CNN for dealing with image classification. The online incident detection was realized by using the time sliding window technique. For testing the performance, this paper develops an incident generation simulation model via a microscopic simulation platform VISSIM. The effectiveness and efficiency are demonstrated by several experiments through the simulation and based on the traffic demand estimated by true traffic flow.

articleTitle: ReachNet : Reachability maps in the presence of obstacles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: Calculating an accurate representation of a manipulator’s capabilities supports motion planning and control tasks. The reachability index is one of the measures used to represent a manipulator’s capabilities within the workspace but the impact of obstacles on the reachability index is not extensively explored. The aim of this manuscript was to evaluate the methods of calculating an accurate reachability index distribution amidst environment obstacles. We propose and evaluate two methods for calculating the reachability index distribution where the machine learning approach came to be the faster method which allowed the model to be applicable in real-time mobile base placement of mobile manipulators. The neural network model may also be used for calculating other distributions of workspace quality measures.

articleTitle: ViNavUT: Vison Based Navigation System for Unmanned Tractor in Airport
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: Airplane towing operations in the apron demand seamless cooperation of multiple operators, thus usually face several challenges including high manpower cost, poor safety and low efficiency. To address these problems, ViNavUT, a vision based navigation system for unmanned tow tractor has been proposed, where only one camera is leveraged to perceive environment and derive a low-price but robust autonomous navigation solution. ViNavUT consists of three main modules. Object detection and segmentation: a multi-object detection and tracking has been utilized to perceive the dynamic entities in the apron. And image segmentation is also used to achieve pixel level classification. Vision based object localization: benefiting from the segmentation results, a refined depth estimation method based on the pinhole camera model has been proposed to determine accurate localization of the objects for path planning. Adaptive navigation: motion predictions of surrounding objects are taken into consideration by path planning to realize a robust autonomous navigation adaptively. Extensive experiments have been conducted to verify its efficacy, and the experimental results prove that ViNavUT is a potentially robust and cost affordable navigation solution for autonomous apron towing operation.

articleTitle: Robust Day and Night Object Detection Based on Heterogeneous Sensors and Information Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: Object detection and localization is now an important component in autonomous driving-related applications, in which the technology based on traditional RGB cameras has become increasingly mature. However, the detection ability of RGB cameras is greatly affected by lighting conditions, such as in a dim environment at night, the information available in RGB images may not be rich enough. We find that thermal infrared images and 3D point clouds from LiDAR can make up for the lack of light and capture more information missing from visible light images. Therefore, we propose a method to fuse RGB images, thermal images and 3D point clouds to facilitate accurate detection in both day and night. Experimental results show that this fusion method improves the detection performance.

articleTitle: Reservoir Computing in Rehabilitation Video Analyses
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: Spatio-temporal information processing is fundamental in rehabilitation video analyses. Current strategies for spatio-temporal pattern recognition usually involve explicit feature extraction followed by feature aggregation, which requires a large amount of labeled data. There are two major challenges for recognizing complex spatio-temporal patterns. One is on extracting the representative features; and the other is on extracting the temporal structure, in particular, the temporal order, of image sequences. Reservoir Computing (RC) offers a promising tool by enabling automatic and accurate analyses of complex movement patterns in rehabilitation videos. Unlike traditional machine learning techniques, RC does not require explicit training of the reservoir connections, which is less data- demanding, more resistant to overfilling and easier to implement. The unique properties make it an attractive option for analyzing rehabilitation video data, where patients may experience changes in their movement patterns over time with a large data flow for processing. By analyzing new video data, the reservoir can adapt and refine its output to reflect the patient’s current conditions.

articleTitle: Robot Tele-Operation / Teaching System using VR Device
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: This paper proposes a "robot tele-teaching system using a VR device" as a new robot teaching method to replace the conventional robot teaching method. Currently we still need teach-pendant to teach industrial robots. It is very inconvenient method. Our novel method consists of two robots and a VR device. One robot is on site instead of the operator. A stereo camera is attached to its end of the robot, which realizes a 3D positionand posture obtained from HMD. The operator can then view the images through the HMD as if he/she are on site. The other manipulating robot is equipped with a gripper and can follow the position and orientation of the gripper-like input device held by the operator. This system is equipped with a correction and auto-teaching function that uses the geometric characteristics of the work object. This significantly reduces the time required for operation. In addition, the teaching points obtained by this system have been successfully used for playback in a real environment.

articleTitle: Output Feedback Stabilization for Anti-Stable Wave Equation Governed by Nonlinear ODEs*
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: In this paper, we aim to address anti-stable wave equation driven by nonlinear actuator dynamics. The first part is to design a state feedback controller when all states are available for measurement. Firstly, the PDE transformation with an explicit kernel function is utilized to address anti-stable wave equation, and then the target system is obtained by combining the finite-dimensional backstepping transformation. Subsequently, the exponential stability of the state-feedback closed-loop system is proved by utilizing Lyapunov functional analysis. In fact, the system states are often not fully measurable. Therefore, we adopt the boundary measurable signal to build an observer to recover the state of the ODE subsystem and the PDE subsystem in the second part. Then, an observer-based output feedback controller is proposed, and the exponential stability of the output feedback closed-loop system is established. Finally, the significance of the theoretical results is illustrated via a numerical example.

articleTitle: Integration Controller For Pico Hydro Power Plant Using Fuzzy-PID Flow Control Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: Energy is a critical component in a country's development. Nowadays, research focuses on green technology, particularly renewable energy resources. It includes wind energy, solar energy, and hydropower, abundant and practically limitless in the natural environment. Hydropower, more specifically standalone pico hydro, is not only environmentally friendly, but it is also convenient for end-users in terms of easy onsite installation, lower cost, low maintenance, and site accessibility, as most rural areas do not have grid access, especially for those living in Sabah and Sarawak. The purpose of pico hydro generating power is to keep the plant's output power parameters within acceptable limits. Therefore, it is critical to maintaining the output power parameters for better performance and efficiency by developing an integrated frequency response controller for standalone pico hydro systems. In this study, various controllers were thoroughly discussed during the literature review. This research aimed to design and implement an efficient hydro turbine management unit with integrated control using an intelligent approach to fuzzy-proportional integral derivative (PID) flow control and a PID load controller before analysis and verification. Our results revealed that using an integrated controller on a pico hydro system improves output response in overshoot percentage and peak value. Meanwhile, the simulation showed that the overshoot for mechanical output using the fuzzy-PID controller was slightly higher, at around 0.641%. However, it was lower in terms of rising time, i.e., 889.30 ms, when compared to the conventional PID controller.

articleTitle: High Precision Pallet Detection and Location Algorithm for AGV
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: Automated guided vehicle (AGV) is the primary solution for automated material handling, achieving precise identification and pickup without relying on external aids such as pallet limits, magnetic strips, or fixed paths is a challenging task. This paper proposes a high-precision pallet detection and positioning method based on a depth camera, which can accurately estimate the pallet pose in a factory environment and assist the AGV in completing the pallet picking task. The main contributions are as follows: 1. A pallet recognition method based on geometric feature matching of pallet legs is proposed, which extracts pallet legs through point cloud filtering, segmentation, and clustering, and combines pallet geometry feature detection to achieve a lightweight pallet recognition method. 2. A precise pose calculation method is designed, which quickly processes subsequent data based on the prior pose obtained from the first frame, selectively fuses features of multiple frames, weakens the fluctuations of single-frame data, and enriches the point cloud of pallet support pillars to improve the accuracy of pose calculation. The proposed method has been deployed and implemented on embedded devices , and has been verified and tested in an industrial environment with AGV. The results show that the pallet detection rate can reach 99%, and the positioning accuracy can reach 10mm and 0.5°, which can achieve accurate pallet pose estimation in practical application environments.

articleTitle: Human-to-Robot Handovers via Real-time Video Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: Object handover in human-robot collaboration is a complex task with challenges ranging from perception to robot movement and grasping planning. In this paper, we propose a real-time method for human-to-robot object handover that addresses the challenges of feasibility, safety, and dynamic adjustment. We use 6-DOF grasping pose detection in space to calculate a reasonable grasping scheme from the input object point cloud extracted from an RGB-D camera. To account for dynamic adjustment, we adjust the grasping pose in real-time for slight wobbles of the object and human hand. We also perform collision detection to ensure safety during grasping pose estimation. Our proposed system splits the human and object components from the video input, and uses point cloud processing and segmentation to extract the necessary features for the task. The system is evaluated on a real-world platform with different objects and scenarios, and the results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our approach.

articleTitle: Advancements and Challenges of Information Integration in Swarm Robotics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: Collaborative control methods employed in swarm robotic systems often deal with bulks of information from the local interactions among agents and between the agents and the environment. The efficiency of overall information integration between decentralized and distributed agents can show major impacts on the collective behaviour of the swarm. It is crucial to establish an approach that bridges an existing gap present between realistic swarm robotic system and real-world enforcements. Therefore, this review paper vividly captures the challenges faced in control and information integration mechanisms within swarm robotic systems, and how recent developments enable tangible benefits to multiple industries as a whole. A comprehensive overview on the current advancements and challenges faced in effective sharing of important information via Pheromonal Communication is also presented. Besides, this paper also discusses the recent advancements pertaining to the information integration systems in one of the major swarm robotic system applications, namely the Autonomous Underwater Vehicles. Forthcoming promising applications with good potential to surpass the recent dilemmas were also explored and analyzed at the end of this paper, with discussions on possible gaps to close in order to enable further enhancements on the efficiency of information integration in swarm robotic systems.

articleTitle: A Fleet Management System of Autonomous Electric Street Sweepers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: With autonomous electric street sweeper’s technology sufficiently mature to be deployed, it is imperative to design a practical and cost-effective fleet management system. This paper formulates two problems related to the fleet management of autonomous electric street sweepers. Firstly, the fleet management system requires to determine the optimal fleet size, optimal locations, and quantity of supporting infrastructure such as depots and charging stations. This is combined with optimal master scheduling and routing plans for all the street sweepers in the service area with the objective to minimize overall street sweeper’s operating cost are defined. Secondly, we formulated an arc routing version of dynamic vehicle rescheduling problem which requires adjustments to the original routing plan when unexpected disruption occurs during the execution stage. The paper reviews related studies and put forward some potential approaches to the fleet management system of autonomous street sweepers. Our main objective is to make fleet management of street sweepers easier to understand and to draw more attention from researchers and practitioners.

articleTitle: Drone-to-drone interception path planning by Deep Q-network with Graph Neural Network based (DQN-GNN) model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: With the increasing ubiquity of drones, criminals may also start using drones more frequently. This may necessitate catching these hostile drones with friendly drones. This paper proposes using reinforcement learning to train an agent involving a deep Q-network (DQN) with an underlying GNN-based model to move and intercept a moving target drone. The results from this approach seem to suggest that the use of GNNs with deep reinforcement learning is a feasible way to tackle this problem. With the method proposed in this work, the chaser drone can be trained to intercept the target drone. Furthermore, the chaser drone can catch the target in a reasonable amount of time.

articleTitle: Development Trend of Robotic Exoskeletons
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: Throughout decades of the history of robotic systems development, exoskeleton has always been an intriguing and interesting branch of robotics. For the general population, exoskeletons can help to boost human physical abilities and overcome limitations. In fact, for certain individuals, exoskeletons have become essential in their day-to-day life. In this study, the background and recent advancements in several state-of-the-art robotic exoskeletons are highlighted and reviewed with the intention to shed new lights on the current development of robotic exoskeletons, including active-robotic exoskeletons, passive robotic exoskeletons, hybrid robotic exoskeletons and quasi- passive robotic exoskeletons. Each type of exoskeleton possesses unique characteristics which enables them to be useful in specific use cases. Several limitations and gaps of the study are also identified and discussed for future research and studies. The engineering knowledge and challenges of building robotic exoskeletons and their kinematics are also thoroughly studied and appreciated.

articleTitle: Improved Semantic Segmentation Adversarial Networks Applied to Industrial Production Datasets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: In industrial production, defect detection is a critical task. Traditional methods often require manual visual inspection, which is low in accuracy and time-consuming. As a key technology in the development of deep learning, semantic segmentation can serve as an effective defect detection method, locating the defect position and providing pixel-level semantic segmentation results that describe the shape and size of the defect, significantly improving production efficiency and product quality.Based on the features of the DAGM 2007 industrial optical detection datasets, this paper uses the SegAN network architecture that combines GAN network with semantic segmentation model and makes adjustments and improvements to it. Because low-level semantic information, such as edges and textures, is important for industrial defect detection, more skip connections are introduced to the original architecture to improve the sensitivity of the network to low-level semantic information in the datasets.Experimental results demonstrate that our improvements can effectively improve the Dice and MIoU index of semantic segmentation, achieving significant performance improvement compared to the original architectures.

articleTitle: Enhancing Semiconductor Chip Image Defect Classification Using Deep Learning and Segmented Defect Region Information
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: Due to the rapid development of deep learning networks in recent years, significant progress has been made in the field of semiconductor image processing. As semiconductor chips are the foundation of modern electronic technology and play an irreplaceable role in information storage, communication transmission, control systems, and other aspects, they are even widely used in fields such as medical care, energy, and environmental protection, making them one of the important engines driving social progress and technological development. However, there are many reasons why semiconductor chip image defects may occur, not only during the complex manufacturing process but also due to changes in temperature, humidity, and lighting. Therefore, it is necessary to control various factors during the manufacturing, transportation, and usage of semiconductor chips to minimize the possibility of defects. In order to promptly identify and solve problems, optimize the manufacturing process, avoid wasting materials and human resources due to manufacturing defects, reduce manufacturing costs, ensure the quality and yield of semiconductor chips, and ultimately reduce manufacturing costs, it is crucial to classify semiconductor chip image defects. However, traditional methods for semiconductor defect image classification have poor generalization ability and are not easy to apply to defect classification. To address this issue in complex scenarios, we propose a deep learning method that aggregates semiconductor image information with the segmented defect region information. By merging the information of the segmented image defect region, the model’s learning process is focused on the image area where defects occur, which can more effectively and accurately learn the classification and recognition of the semiconductor image condition, further improving the accuracy of image defect classification. Overall, our method significantly reduces the waste of human resources in defect classification and achieves more accurate and efficient judgment.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control For Production Scheduling Integrating Material Handling In Flexible Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: Production scheduling and material handling are two main optimization problems in flexible manufacturing. This paper constructs a D-timed Petri net (DTPN) for flexible job shop problems and applies model predictive control (MPC) as the optimization solver. Two types of flexibility are included in DTPN, i.e., machine flexibility and route flexibility. Machine flexibility means more than one machine is capable of performing a specific operation. Route flexibility enables modelling the sequence of operations in a job as an arbitrary directed acyclic graph, rather than just a linear sequence. The minimization of makespan (the ultimate completion time for all production jobs) is the objective. To represent makespan in the problem formulation, each place in the DTPN is labelled with a continuous time variable. An update scheme of time variables caused by transitions is proposed. To integrate the material handling problem, the result of material handling is represented by the time variable of material buffer places, which is a type of place in DTPN model utilized in this paper. The receding horizon strategy of MPC is employed to repeatedly solve the optimization problem online until the completion of all the assigned production jobs. By comparing our simulation results with those published in the literature, the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed MPC based on DTPN is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Enhancing Deep Neural Network Corruption Robustness using Evolutionary Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: A robust image classifier can model a classification function well and has subliminal impacts on classification performance when the input data is corrupted in some ways. Many popular classifiers based on deep neural networks (DNN) are trained using back-propagation (BP) that explicitly computes the gradient of a loss function. However, the BP-trained DNN shows poor performance on diverse types of image corruption. In this work, we propose the use of an evolutionary algorithm, differential evolution (DE), to evolve a population of BP pre-trained DNNs and examine whether the evolution improves DNNs’ classification robustness against various types of corruption. Specifically, pre-trained MobileNet and ResNet on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet are evolved using DE. Despite no change in network architecture and loss function, DE empirically enhances DNNs’ corruption robustness, in terms of mean Corruption Error (mCE), in almost all types of corruptions in CIFAR-100-C (18 out of 18 corruptions with ResNet-18) and Imagenet-C (18 out of 19 corruptions with MobileNetV2, except for impulse noise). The preliminary results and findings have implications for refining the robustness of BP-pre-trained DNNs.

articleTitle: Wafer Map Defect Recognition and Accurate Localization Based on Defect Completion Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: In order to achieve high quality monitoring and yield management, wafer defect detection for key processes has become a common consensus in advanced semiconductor manufacturing. The accuracy of wafer defect detection has a great impact on the efficiency of semiconductor process production and the traceability of faults in the production line. With the development of the semiconductor industry, most of the wafer fault defects are mixed defect types, which pose a great challenge to wafer defect detection. For the precise detection of wafer defect location in hybrid mode, we propose a novel method, which combines the wafer defect segmentation of the deep learning model and Defect Completion (DC) algorithm, which is the post-processing algorithm of wafer defect segmentation, to complete the completion of the discrete area after segmentation, to achieve higher accurate defect location. We have carried out extensive experiments on the self-made dataset, and the experimental results have demonstrated the effectiveness of the algorithm. Compared to the methods without using the proposed DC algorithm, our method has achieved remarkable performance improvements.

articleTitle: Wafer Map Defect Patterns Semi-Supervised Classification Using Latent Vector Representation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: As the globalization of semiconductor design and manufacturing processes continues, the demand for defect detection during integrated circuit fabrication stages is becoming increasingly critical, playing a significant role in enhancing the yield of semiconductor products. Traditional wafer map defect pattern detection methods involve manual inspection using electron microscopes to collect sample images, which are then assessed by experts for defects. This approach is labor-intensive and inefficient. Consequently, there is a pressing need to develop a model capable of automatically detecting defects as an alternative to manual operations. In this paper, we propose a method that initially employs a pre-trained VAE model to obtain the fault distribution information of the wafer map. This information serves as guidance, combined with the original image set for semi-supervised model training. During the semi-supervised training, we utilize a teacher-student network for iterative learning. The model presented in this paper is validated on the benchmark dataset WM-811K wafer dataset. The experimental results demonstrate superior classification accuracy and detection performance compared to state-of-the-art models, fulfilling the requirements for industrial applications. Compared to the original architecture, we have achieved significant performance improvement.

articleTitle: APC: Automatic Passenger Counting and Seat Occupancy Detection for Sightseeing Tram based on 3D LiDAR and Camera
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: Enhancing the efficiency and safety of public transportation is crucial, and automatic passenger counting (APC) and seat occupancy detection play a significant role in achieving this goal. However, current APC methods, which rely on infrared and pressure sensors or vision, face challenges in accuracy, installation, and occlusion handling, particularly for low-top, open-air sightseeing trams. Although some studies have explored the use of 3D-optical time-of-flight (TOF) sensors and millimeter-wave radar, the application of 3D LiDAR in APC remains largely unexplored. To address these challenges, we present a novel algorithm that integrates 3D LiDAR and RGB cameras to accurately count passengers and detect seat occupancy in open-air sightseeing trams. Our proposed system holds significant promise for enhancing the management and operation of sightseeing trams in tourist areas, elevating visitor experiences, and fostering sustainable tourism.

articleTitle: Hybrid metaheuristics for integrated dispatching and conflict-free vehicle routing of automated guided vehicles in flexible manufacturing systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: Automated guided vehicles (AGVs) are pervasively used for transportation in flexible manufacturing systems (FMSs), in which production scheduling, vehicle dispatching, and conflict-free vehicle routing (CVR) are three pivot sub-problems. Even though these sub-problems are interrelated, they are often solved sequentially due to their complexity. By combining the particle swarm optimization (PSO), genetic algorithm (GA), and A* algorithm, this paper proposed a metaheuristic (HPSO-GA) that can solve these three sub-problems simultaneously. A hybridization method, specially designed for FJSPCVR, can let PSO compensate for GA’s weakness and vice versa by using their complementary strengths. A modified A* algorithm based on time windows is embedded in the HPSO-GA to find the shortest route on the time domain and resolve conflicts along the path. The proposed HPSO-GA is implemented on a new benchmark with a more complex roadmap and larger manufacturing job scale compared to a former benchmark used in flexible job shop problems. Simulation results indicate that HPSO-GA is applicable for solving integrated scheduling problems in FMSs from an engineering perspective.

articleTitle: Magnetic Field-Aided Global Localization in Repetitive Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: Geometrically repetitive environments (e.g., corridors, indoor/semi-indoor car parks, warehouses) contain highly similar structures and few distinct geometric features. Such environment is one of the most critical and challenging scenarios for mobile robots or autonomous vehicles to perform localization or Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) tasks, where the robots/vehicles are extremely easy to be mis-localized to wrong places or even get lost. Existing solutions for such scenarios either rely heavily on pre-deployed infrastructures (e.g., WiFi routers, UWB beacons) which are inflexible and hard to maintain; or rely on single-modal (e.g., LiDAR, camera) based localization methods, whose observation module is not capable enough to acquire distinctive geometric information. The ambient magnetic field (MF) has exhibited high distinctiveness and ubiquity at different location, which makes it a viable alternative to the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) signal in the local environments. Thus, this paper proposes a novel probabilistic magnetic field (MF)-aided 3D LiDAR global localization system for mobile robots operating in geometrically repetitive and ambiguous environments. The proposed system mainly consists of: 1) MF-based initial pose estimation, and 2) Enhanced particle filtering (EPF)-based pose determination. Extensive experimental results demonstrate the practical utility of the proposed system in accurately localizing the mobile robot in real-world GNSS-challenged repetitive scenarios.

articleTitle: Three Dimensional Multi-Camera Multi-Target Re-identifications by 3D Point Cloud and Successive Convex Hull
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: This paper discusses the re-identifications (Re-ID) of multiple targets or objects of interest (OOI) across multiple non-aligned cameras in three-dimensions (3D) without referring to environment. The situation can be aerial targets, such as birds, seen by other aerial observers, such as drones. This is also suitable for identical targets where re-identification by appearance is impossible. The challenges are to overcome occlusions of those targets, and identify their positions in 3D. We assume the camera positions and poses (orientations) are known, at least 2 cameras are near each other. We apply Pseudo-stereo camera approximation to get the targets’ 3D position (3D point clouds). Then, we can transform the 3D point clouds from global view to other cameras’ view for matching. The subsequent matching (re-identification) can be done through Successive Convex Hull and/or nearest neighbour matching. This proposed technique shows better accuracy than other topology-based technique as the technique can overcome targets’ self occlusions and provide unique solutions. The accuracy is close to 100% for 3 or more cameras.

Author Keywords: Three dimensional Multi Camera Multi Target

articleTitle: Mixed Traffic Optimization With Platooning Technology Based on Stackelberg Game Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a game theoretical decision making framework for mixed traffic with platooning technology. Different from considering an interaction between multiple automated vehicles (AVs) in a same lane and an ego car (EC) on the other lane, we first use platooning technology to assemble the AVs to harvest the traffic efficacy. Therefore, the number of players shrinks to two, which could save plenty of computation time. However, the platooning technology offers multiple gap choices for the EC and the technology is reluctant to the EC’s lane-changing behaviour, which are not considered in the previous literature. To cope with the above problems, a Stackelberg game is used to generate a proper decision for the platoon against the cut-in behaviour, taking into account the driving safety and ride comfort. To obtain mixed traffic optimization, we then adapt the platoon’s acceleration range to discourage the EC’s cut-in intention by increasing the cost of the EC side when the cut-in happens. A sufficient condition on the platoon’s acceleration range which ensures the EC to stay in its initial lane as the optimal strategy based on Stackelberg game is derived. Numerical examples confirm the outcomes of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Model Predictive Control of a Dual-Axis Tilting Quadcopter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: The dual-axis tilting quadcopter holds great promise for applications that demand both high performance and full actuation in a 6DOF Cartesian task space; however, control system design is complicated by its complex dynamics and over-actuation. In this paper, we propose a real-time optimization-based framework for controlling this system. Our formulation, which combines Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) with a control allocation stage, allows the optimizer to fully exploit the rotors’ tilt actuation despite their strongly nonlinear dynamics, input constraints, and actuator redundancy. Numerical simulation is provided to illustrate the performance of the proposed control algorithm.

articleTitle: Evaluating Optimization Approaches for Deep-Reinforcement-Learning-based Navigation Agents
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: In recent years, Deep Reinforcement learning has made remarkable progress in various application areas such as control of robots and vehicles, simulation, and natural language processing. In recent years, various research works applied DRL to conduct different kinds of tasks for autonomous navigation of vehicles and robots such as lane changing, cruise control, or obstacle avoidance. However, DRL training is still a tedious and difficult process due to long training times, catastrophic forgetfulness and the myopic nature of DRL agents. In this paper, we integrate and explore the effect of a variety of state-of-the-art optimization approaches for DRL agents such as imitation learning, behavior cloning, frame stacking, and hindsight replay for autonomous obstacle avoidance. We evaluate the effect of each of these changes to the DRL agent in terms of training- as well as navigational performance. The resulting agents are compared against baseline approaches without those optimizations and we found an increase in navigational performance for some of these methods while other optimization approaches surprisingly resulted in decreased performing. The findings of this paper should aid in development of DRL approaches for autonomous navigation approaches.

articleTitle: Adaptive Modelling for Anomaly Detection and Defect Diagnosis in Semiconductor Smart Manufacturing: A Domain-specific AutoML
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: Early detection and diagnosis of the defect in semiconductor wafer production offer significant advantages for various advanced solutions in smart manufacturing. However, inherent challenges exist, including the absence of physical interpretation for features, data imbalance, heterogeneous and missing data. This study proposes a domain-specific AutoML (termed AutoClassifier) for anomaly detection and defect diagnosis to self-learn the optimal models for semiconductor defects, enabling end-to-end machine learning, which integrates four main contributions. Firstly, feature engineering, which includes data preprocessing, extraction, and selection based on the SECOM dataset, a series of features are extracted by interpolation methods after data cleaning. Then, we use a feature selection approach that pinpoints valuable features through the elimination-based model reliance importance technique. Secondly, unsupervised anomaly detection, estimate and judge the defect’s categories, Process-induced defects or anomalies. Thirdly, based on the hyperparameters optimization algorithm Hyperband, the algorithm auto-selection and hyperparameter auto-tuning are self-learned to generate the best defect-classifying results. Fourthly, the focal loss integrates into state-of-the-art classifiers LightGBM and XGBoost, which focus on settling down widespread data imbalance in semiconductor wafer production. The comparison and selection of the algorithm prove focal loss is effective, which has improved the overall F1 score from 85% to 92.3%. The results show that AutoClassifier is useful in tackling the challenges of imbalanced process data, and effectively detects and diagnoses semiconductor defects.

articleTitle: AutoML with Focal Loss for Defect Diagnosis and Prognosis in Smart Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: Reliable defect diagnosis and prognosis for production lines are of great benefit in a range of advanced solutions towards smart manufacturing and yield optimization. However, inherent challenges exist, especially imbalanced data, missing value, and knowledge-related feature engineering. This study proposes a domain-specific automated machine learning (AutoML) method to self-learn the optimal models for defect diagnosis and prognosis. Firstly, a tree-based AutoML with focal loss (termed AutoGBM) is proposed based on XGBoost and Bayesian Optimization to improve imbalanced learning performance. Secondly, the AutoGBM system includes a hybrid feature learning mechanism based on fast feature filtering and recursive elimination, by which the key factors for defect diagnosis can be unveiled. Meanwhile, the proposed feature learning can identify the optimal interpolation preprocess to tackle missing data. Thirdly, based on Bayesian optimization, hyperparameter autotuning is conducted to generate the best prognostic results. Herein, SECOM data is used for test-bedding. Experimental results have demonstrated that AutoGBM is reliable and promising to diagnose key factors and predict defects in an automated way, as well as achieve adaptive model updates according to changes in manufacturing lines.

articleTitle: A Study on 28 GHz Power Amplifiers for Industrial Revolution 4.0 Compatible 5G NR FR2 IoT Transceivers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems (CIS) and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (RAM)
abstract: Industrial Revolution 4.0 (IR 4.0) has always been a hot topic to be discussed along with the Internet of Things (IoT). With current 5G wireless technology, IoT systems are able to be connected even wider and can cover more applications such as AI/ML, edge computing, and smart factories. 5G NR have standardized FR1 and FR2 bands, and FR2 have the potential to establish the network for Industrial-IoT (I-IoT) system. Although FR2 have limits on transmission distance, a power amplifier (PA) located in the transmitter circuit is able to boost the distance with its produced high output power. In this paper, we will investigate the potential of 5G NR FR2 28 GHz for I-IoT applications and review the available state-of-the-art PA designs and their available modulation scheme. Each PA design in this article will be discussed, and compared. This paper will serve as a small review for authors to design PA for I-IoT applications in the 5G NR FR2 band.
